key: Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy: therein let them rejoice. It is better than what they hoard.
s: Just after an exhortation and a balm for the breasts is announced to mankind, the Prophet is told what to say; al-Tabari, on 10:58, reads the bounty as Islam and the mercy as the Qur’an, together worth more than this world’s wealth and treasure.

evidence.words: ﴿بفضل الله﴾ ، أيها الناس، الذي تفضل به عليكم، وهو الإسلام، فبيَّنه لكم، ودعاكم إليه = ﴿وبرحمته﴾ ، التي رحمكم بها، فأنزلها إليكم، فعلَّمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون من كتابه، وبصَّركم بها معالم دينكم، وذلك القرآن = ﴿فبذلك فليفرحوا هو خير مما يجمعون﴾ ، يقول: فإن الإسلام الذي دعاهم إليه، والقرآن الذي أنزله عليهم، خيرٌ مما يجمعون من حُطَام الدنيا وأموالها وكنوزها
evidence.gloss: “In the bounty of God”, O people, with which He has favoured you: that is Islam, which He made plain to you and called you to; “and in His mercy”, with which He had mercy on you and sent down to you, teaching you from His Book what you did not know: that is the Qur’an. “Therein let them rejoice; it is better than what they hoard”: the Islam He called them to and the Qur’an He sent down are better than the debris of this world, its wealth and its treasures, that they amass.

reason: Second judgement with the refutation in hand. Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Yunus 10:58, at 1421). Plain sense faithful to day.js: 10:57 announces to mankind an exhortation, a balm for the breasts, a guidance and a mercy, and 10:58 opens with Say. Re-read al-Tabari on 10:58 in the packet: his own gloss (qala Abu Jafar) makes the bounty Islam and the mercy the Quran, then one predicate on the joined subject: Islam and the Quran are better than the debris of this world, its wealth and treasures. He reports the reverse pairing without ruling on it. The refuter is right that each worth more distributes a comparison his words make jointly; changed each to together. Nothing else changed; entry-check ok, 44 words, evidence re-found verbatim in the packet. Evidence words re-copied from the packet output character for character (the earlier copy had its shadda and fatha in the other order).
